story.title: COP31 Climate Summit Fails to Adopt Agreement Amid Fossil Fuel Dispute
story.summary: The COP31 climate summit concluded without adopting a final agreement, as nations could not reach consensus on including fossil fuels in the discussions. The summit was extended in an attempt to finalize a deal, but criticism arose from European nations, small island states, and activists regarding the lack of fossil fuel references in the draft agreement.

event_overview.title: About Climate Change
event_overview.subject: Climate Change
event_overview.summary: COP31 was the 2026 United Nations Climate Change Conference, the annual negotiating session for parties to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC). It brought governments together in Antalya, Türkiye, alongside accredited observers and other stakeholders, to negotiate and advance international action on emissions reductions, adaptation and climate finance under the UN climate treaties.

facts.label: Dates and venue
facts.value: The conference was scheduled for 9-20 November 2026 at the Antalya EXPO Center in Soğucaksu, Antalya, Türkiye.

facts.label: Institutional basis
facts.value: COP31 was the 31st session of the Conference of the Parties to the 1992 UNFCCC, the framework treaty that underpins the international climate-negotiation process and is the parent treaty to the 2015 Paris Agreement.

facts.label: Meeting format
facts.value: The gathering also convened CMP21, the meeting of parties to the Kyoto Protocol, and CMA8, the meeting of parties to the Paris Agreement; these linked bodies consider matters under their respective treaties.

facts.label: Hosts and leadership
facts.value: Türkiye hosted the conference, with Murat Kurum nominated as COP31 President; Australia’s Chris Bowen served as President of Negotiations under the Türkiye-Australia partnership arrangements.

facts.label: Participants and access
facts.value: Parties to the UNFCCC sent leaders and negotiators, while accredited observer groups—including UN bodies, intergovernmental organizations, NGOs, business representatives, scientists, Indigenous Peoples and youth—could participate under UNFCCC procedures. Official negotiating meetings were held in the registered-participant Blue Zone; the host-managed Green Zone was intended for public-facing activities.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline follows the conference’s opening and its reported collapse over fossil-fuel language; it does not attempt to catalogue every negotiation text, side event, national statement or issue discussed during COP31.

related_stories.title: COP31 Climate Talks Fail as EU and Others Reject Final Deal
related_stories.summary: The COP31 climate talks have collapsed after the European Union and other parties rejected a final draft agreement, citing its inadequacy in addressing global warming. This marks a significant setback, reminiscent of the last major failure at the Copenhagen talks in 2009.

related_stories.title: COP31 Climate Talks Conclude Without Agreement on Fossil Fuels or Funding
related_stories.summary: The COP31 climate summit ended without a consensus after two weeks of negotiations, as delegates failed to reach an agreement on phasing out fossil fuels and providing financial support for vulnerable countries. Disagreements over the inclusion of the term 'fossil fuels' and climate funding proved insurmountable, leading to disappointment among participants.

related_stories.title: Trump Directs Contractors to Withhold Information from Congress
related_stories.summary: President Trump has issued an executive order instructing federal contractors to consult with the White House before responding to inquiries from Congress. The order mandates that any communications deemed 'privileged' by the administration should be withheld from Congress. This move is seen as a response to anticipated oversight efforts from Democrats set to take control of Congress in January.

related_stories.title: Israeli Opposition Leader Condemns Attacks on Palestinian Villages as 'Jewish Terrorism'
related_stories.summary: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has condemned a series of arson attacks on Palestinian villages in the occupied West Bank, labeling them as 'Jewish terrorism.' The attacks involved Israeli settlers setting fire to vehicles and properties in multiple locations. In response, Israeli authorities have initiated an investigation into the incidents.
